probes.timeoutJustification: the band-3 component-system pass only runs inside a loaded game space, so an attach-window run would report every check COULD-NOT-DETERMINE and buy nothing. The probe does not hold the launch open for the deadline: it settles 3 s, then files as soon as it has either 120 callback invocations or 600 ticks with the registration standing -- both are determinations. On a launch that reaches a match it finishes seconds after the match does and the harness's complete-on-report ends the launch then. 180 s rather than 120 s only because the registration cannot even be attempted until a game space exists, which is later than the reads W1-M's probe takes.
probes.why: W2-F's panel, timeline and browser all draw from one band-3 CS callback, and whether that callback exists at all is unobservable offline. Three questions, and the first two are the ones the packet stands on. (1) DOES THE REGISTRATION LAND: scheme+0x610 read immediately before and immediately after the shipping CS.GAMESPACE_REGISTER_UPDATE call. The registrar has no failure path and no return value, so the record count moving is the ONLY evidence it appended. (2) DOES THE CALLBACK FIRE, AND ON WHICH THREAD: raw GetCurrentThreadId per invocation against the tick's own thread id, plus the raw per-thread CTaskKernel dispatch flag at TlsGetValue(idx)+1840 -- because ImGui is not thread-safe and W1-M's last open [U] is exactly whether a CS node can be handed to a worker. (3) the live clock ceiling at clock+0x60 with the mean frameDeltaUs beside it, which turns 66666 into an actual fast-forward ceiling for this machine and retires the panel's fallback to the constant. GUARDS offline-bit-lock, and the declaration is now a MECHANISM rather than a promise. An earlier version of this descriptor declared the guard while probe_ui.dll installed nothing: offlinelock::Apply() runs only from WorkerMain, and only bootstrap::Attach starts that thread, so linking replay_bootstrap put all thirteen of its sources into this binary and reached none of them. The harness cannot see inside a DLL, so launch 10 would have run -offline past the login window believing it was protected -- the worst shape a guard takes, against the one constraint on this project that has already been breached once. probe_ui.cpp's DllMain now calls bootstrap::Attach, and tests/ui/CMakeLists.txt already names replay_bootstrap for it. CALLING Attach IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and this descriptor does not pretend otherwise: Attach returns false at coexist::ClaimInstance before it reaches CreateThread(WorkerMain), so a probe that loses the instance claim in a shared plugins folder installs no lock at all. The probe therefore READS offlinelock::Current().state -- which lives in shared memory precisely so a module that did not win the install race still reports what the process actually did -- and FAILS the check offline-bit-lock-held when the process is not protected. Locked and AlreadyLockedInProcess are both held; every RefusedBy* value is a state in which the lock was ATTEMPTED and is NOT held, which is why the predicate is a disjunction and not 'state != NotAttempted'. tests/ui/offlinelock_held.h is that predicate in one place and tests/ui/test_panel.cpp exercises it over the whole enum offline, asserting exactly two of the nine defined states are held and that a value outside the range is not. carriesBootstrap true, and it is now true of the LINKED IMAGE and not only of the build graph: coexist::ClaimInstance is genuinely reached, so this probe contends for the single-instance claim and must not share a launch with another bootstrap-carrying probe. SECOND DEFECT, FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST, AND IT INVALIDATED EVERY RUN THIS PROBE COULD EVER HAVE MADE: modreg::InitAll has exactly one caller and it is inside that same WorkerMain, so without bootstrap::Attach this probe's own ProbeInit never ran, ProbeTick never ran, csregister never registered, and all three reads above could only ever report COULD-NOT-DETERMINE. The probe was structurally incapable of answering its own questions, and the call that installs the guard is the call that fixes that.
probes.scope:
ESTABLISHES the three reads above on THIS profile only. The dispatch flag is per-thread engine state and a different profile may schedule differently, so a clean thread result here is not a claim about the VR path. It MEASURES THE SHIPPING CODE: the DLL links src/ui/csregister.cpp itself plus the shipped bootstrap and the shipped tick, so a wrong order key or a wrong scheme offset in the product is a wrong one here too -- a reimplementation could have got either right by accident. IT DRAWS NOTHING: no NRadGui call is made, so this says nothing about whether a GUI frame is open at band 3, only about whether and where the callback runs. It does NOT answer w2f-gui-frame-open-at-stage0, which needs a trampoline on GUI.STARTFRAME that this probe declines to install; the panel does not depend on it, because band 3 is inside the open frame under both of the readings that question separates. Every check reports Ok, Failed or COULD-NOT-DETERMINE and `checked` counts only the first two, so a launch that never reaches a match reports checked=0 rather than a confident nothing. A registration that lands and never fires is reported as FAILED with the band trap excluded by the key actually used -- that is a determination about the engine, not a failed read.

The probe still FILES when refused, from its static initialiser, and says which; but it files COULD-NOT-DETERMINE, and this is the read the panel's existence depends on.
